reference: Ahuja, R. K., Magnanti, T. L., & Orlin, J. B. (1993). Network Flows: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications.
natural_language_example: A logistics network moves several product classes over directed links between cities. For every city and product, there may be supply, demand, or neither. For each directed link and product there is a per-unit shipping cost and a product-specific capacity. Each directed link also has a joint capacity across all products. The decision is the continuous nonnegative amount of each product shipped on each directed link. The objective is to minimize total shipment cost while preserving city-product flow balance and respecting both joint link capacities and product-specific link capacities. This is a continuous multi-commodity flow LP, not a fixed-charge network design model with binary arc activation.
